title: Affordable Sinskey Hook Goniotomy and Cataract Surgery in Black and Afro-Latino Patients Diagnosed with Glaucoma: Retrospective Real-World One-Year Results

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license, MDPI)

indication: mild to moderate open-angle or narrow-angle glaucoma and related diagnoses (primary open-angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension, angle-closure glaucoma, glaucoma suspects, narrow angles, pigmentary glaucoma), predominantly Black and Afro-Latino patients; phacoemulsification combined with goniotomy using a 200-µm Sinskey hook; retrospective single-centre series of eyes that completed 1 year of follow-up

groups.description: All eyes after phacoemulsification with Sinskey hook goniotomy; only the whole cohort is tabulated over time (Table 3)

series.notes: mean ± SD (asterisks mark significance and are ignored); rows 'Baseline', 'Post-operative day 1', '1 month', '3 months', '6 months', '1 year'; day 1 = 1/30.4375 months; per-visit n not reported; analysis set restricted by the authors to eyes that completed 1 year of follow-up

exclusions.what: Table 3 columns 3 to 5 (medications, BCVA, visual field)
exclusions.reason: medication counts are mentioned in notes only; BCVA and visual field are not IOP
duplicate of the Table 3 baseline row; the Table 3 cell is cited
demographics, race and spherical equivalent, not IOP series

exclusions.what: IOP reduction percentage, medication-free proportion and IOP spike counts in the text
exclusions.reason: changes and proportions are not extracted when the absolute IOP series is tabulated; counts are not admissible

exclusions.what: End-of-surgery pressurisation of the eye (Procedure section)

notes: Tonometer: not stated in the article.

Reference: baseline collected on medically treated eyes without preoperative washout (Results), recorded as preoperative_medicated; some eyes used no IOP-lowering medication at baseline (Table 1 rows R9 to R13).
All glaucoma medications were stopped in the operated eye immediately after surgery and restarted as clinically indicated (Methods).
Inclusion required completion of the 1-year follow-up (completers set, not an outcome-defined exclusion); kept as ordinary attrition.
Mixed diagnoses are pooled in the only tabulated series; no subgroup is tabulated over time.
Table 3 column 3 tabulates the number of medications at each visit; not extracted.
